key_insight: AI2-BPSP predicts the atomistic microstructure and diffraction signature of amorphous poly(1,3-dioxolane) by simulating its living polymerization from first principles.
engineering_relevance: This enables structure-guided design and validation of ultra-high-molecular-weight recyclable polymers whose mechanical performance depends on amorphous chain packing that experiments alone cannot fully resolve.
method: Simulated living cationic ring-opening polymerization under experimental synthetic conditions.
Used machine-learning force fields trained on van der Waals-corrected hybrid DFT.
Partitioned X-ray and neutron diffraction into monomer and growing-polymer contributions across chain lengths.
evidence_signal: The predicted diffraction feature at q ≈ 1.5–1.6 Å⁻1 separates into a monomer peak that decays with monomer consumption and a polymer peak that grows with chain length.
watch_item: The predictions are statistically and computationally intensive, and direct experimental validation is still needed for the chain-length-resolved diffraction assignments.
paper_title: Bottom-Up Prediction of Amorphous Poly(1,3-dioxolane) using Ab Initio Reactive Machine-Learning Force Fields
